extracted.intended_audience: educated general readers and students of sociology/political theory (readers of Popular Science Monthly)
extracted.subtask_description: An 1880 essay by Herbert Spencer outlining conceptual criteria for what constitutes a society and distinguishing two general kinds of social organization (spontaneous/division-of-labor vs. conscious/governmental), with implications for the nature and function of political organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Society defined by cooperation (not mere juxtaposition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere gathering of individuals into a group does not constitute them a society. A society, in the sociological sense, is formed only when, besides juxtaposition, there is cooperation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cooperation exists when members combine energies to achieve some common end or apportion different activities to different persons so that the wants of each are better satisfied by uniting efforts than by acting alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation implies organization
rubrics_metrics.description: If acts are to be effectually combined, there must be arrangements under which they are adjusted in their times, amounts, and characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social organization is necessary as a means to concerted action — organization provides the arrangements that coordinate cooperative acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two kinds of social organization (spontaneous vs. conscious)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a spontaneous cooperation which grows up without thought during the pursuit of private ends; and there is a cooperation which, consciously devised, implies distinct recognition of public ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although generally coexisting and interfused, the two kinds differ in origins, traits, and ways they are established and carried on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spontaneous/industrial organization arises from private ends (division of labor)
rubrics_metrics.description: When cooperation is effected by exchange of services and the division of labor, organization grows by experience of mutual facilitation in living and from the effort of individuals to secure profit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such organization (employer/employee relations, agencies adjusting supplies) usually lacks coercive power and regulates activities largely by communicating information that stimulates or restrains, rather than by deliberate public-purpose control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conscious/governmental organization arises for public ends and involves coercion
rubrics_metrics.description: Cooperation which unites actions of individuals for purposes immediately concerning the whole society is conscious, not wholly a matter of choice, and is carried on by organizations that constrain individual wills in furtherance of public ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From defense against other groups to the maintenance of a militant organization and government, agencies evolve that force citizens to labor more or less largely for public ends and restrain individual activities to preserve social safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrast of instrumental aims: private vs. public welfare
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial (spontaneous) organization directly seeks and subserves the welfares of individuals and indirectly the welfare of society; governmental (conscious) organization directly seeks and subserves the welfare of society and indirectly the welfares of individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Efforts for self-preservation by units originate spontaneous organization; efforts for self-preservation by the aggregate originate conscious organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of authority and graded organization in militant/governmental systems
rubrics_metrics.description: In militant organization (e.g., army) and the governmental structures that support it, grades and divisions cooperate under consciously established regulations that override individual volitions and control individuals by motives preventing spontaneous action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recognized superior (warrior/leader) exercises influence beyond group opinion; as authority becomes established it furthers combined action necessary for defense and public ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulative agencies evolve from joint wills to definite authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies that maintain militant organization and direct government are established over citizens first by the joint wills of the entire group and afterward more definitely by the will of a regulative agency which the group evolves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This evolution converts group consensus into a definite controlling agency whose will constrains individuals for public purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of labor as an unconscious source of complex organization
rubrics_metrics.description: The elaborate division of labor and its regulating agencies have arisen unintentionally in the pursuit of private gain, only later being recognized as an evolving system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specializations and agencies that regulate production/distribution establish themselves by conducing to profit and by communicating information that aligns supply with demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political organization characterized as the consciously purposive part of social organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Political organization is to be understood as that part of social organization which consciously carries (on public ends) — i.e., the portion evolved for deliberate public-purpose coordination and control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicitly contrasted with non-political social organization, political organization entails conscious design, regulative agencies, and coercive elements directed at preserving the society as a whole.
